title: Contract Pricing Agreement Final Rebate Check: Credit Exposure Holdback
content:
Credit exposure holdback on a Contract Pricing Agreement final rebate check

The exposure holdback follows the receivable balance of the customer's Commercial Credit Account (a customer holds one) as a share of its credit limit, both as that account's record shows them.

| Receivable balance as a share of the credit limit | Exposure holdback |
|---|---|
| 0.9 or more | 5 percent of the unpaid rebate balance |
| At least 0.75 and below 0.9 | 2.5 percent of the unpaid rebate balance |
| Below 0.75, or no credit limit on record | None |

The amount is held back from the unpaid rebate balance before the final check's floor at 0.00, its rounding to the cent and its minimum payout test are applied; what is held back stays in the rebate balance.

Hypothetical cases: receivable balance 45000.00 on a credit limit of 50000.00 is a share of 0.9 and holds back 5 percent; 37500.00 on the same limit is exactly 0.75 and holds back 2.5 percent; 37499.99 holds back nothing.
